root_cause.text: In `fsnotify_prepare_user_wait()`, when `fsnotify_get_mark_safe()` returns false for a mark belonging to an unrelated group (i.e., a mark being removed from a different group), the function immediately releases the SRCU lock and fails, causing the entire permission event to be bypassed (false positive granting of permission).
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "fsnotify_get_mark_safe() may return false for a mark on an unrelated group, which results in bypassing the permission check." The patch adds logic to skip over such unrelated marks instead of failing, only failing if the failed mark belongs to the current group. The original code (before patch) unconditionally went to `fail` on a `false` return from `fsnotify_get_mark_safe()`.
